issues.title: Unbound line-search cap
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm's input supplies \(\lambda_{\max}>0\), while Step 6 requires \(\bar\lambda_{\max}\). Consequently, the initial trial step and hence the backtracking sequence are not literally determined by the old input.
issues.overall_effect: The procedure is not executable as written, and formal guarantees explicitly concerning sequences generated by that algorithm cannot be applied literally until the cap identifier is bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use one identifier for the line-search cap. For example, change the input in Step 1 to “bar lambda_max > 0” and use that same supplied quantity in Step 6 as the initial trial step. No proof or guarantee otherwise needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old algorithm plainly supplies one positive line-search cap, and the barred symbol in Step 6 has no separate definition or mathematical role. Binding it to the supplied cap is uniquely forced by the surrounding algorithm and repairs no inference or construction beyond the transcriptional identifier mismatch.

issues.title: Invalid uniform coefficient bound in the square-summability proof
issues.failure_explanation: The old lemma defines \(\lambda_{\max}=\sqrt{4/(3\delta tL)-1/2}-1\). Substitution gives \(c(\lambda_{\max},\delta t,L)=0\), not a positive number. Moreover, \(\lambda_{\min}=\min_n\lambda_n\) need not exist or be positive for an infinite sequence, so the printed coefficient in ineq:quad_A is not established as uniformly positive. The valid preceding per-step coefficient is instead \([\alpha\lambda+c(\lambda,\delta t,L)]/(1+\lambda)^2\).
issues.overall_effect: The displayed telescoping estimate does not prove square summability as written, removing an input used by the smooth global-convergence theorem and its local-rate theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let r = sqrt(4/(3 delta t L) - 1/2) - 1 and use the actual per-step coefficient q(lambda) = [alpha lambda + 4/(3 delta t) - L/2 - L(1+lambda)^2]/(1+lambda)^2. This extends continuously to [0,r], with q(0) > 0 and q(r) = alpha r/(1+r)^2 > 0, so gamma := min_{0 <= lambda <= r} q(lambda) is positive. Replace the invalid bound in ineq:quad_A by gamma times ||u^{n+1}-u^n||^2, telescope it, and use gamma in the global-convergence and local-rate constants. No lambda_min is needed.
issues.why_classification: The printed uniformization is mathematically invalid, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the preceding estimate already contains everything needed: a routine compactness check supplies a uniform positive coefficient under the original step-size hypothesis. This local replacement preserves square summability, the global theorem, and the local rate without weakening any guarantee or introducing a new proof mechanism.

issues.title: Incorrect smooth auxiliary-gradient and residual calculation
issues.failure_explanation: For the stated auxiliary function, differentiating the quadratic term gives coefficient \(L+2/(3\delta t)\), not \(L_f/2+1/(3\delta t)\). At iteration \(n+1\), rewriting eq:solve:y:pre:general also gives the BDF residual with coefficient \(2/(3\delta t)\) and the term \(M(y^{n+1}-u^{n+1})\). The old proof instead uses inconsistent BDF coefficients and \(M(y^n-u^n)\). Thus eq:esti:grad:A does not follow from the displayed calculations.
issues.overall_effect: Parts (i) and (iii) of the smooth global theorem lose their relative-error input, and the local-rate argument that uses the same estimate is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the stated auxiliary function with C0 = L + 2/(3 delta t). At iteration n+1 use the exact optimality residual: f(u^{n+1}) = -[2/(3 delta t)](3y^{n+1}-4u^{n+1}+u^n) - [f(u^{n+1})-f(u^n)] - h(y^{n+1}) - M(y^{n+1}-u^{n+1}). Substitution and the stated Lipschitz bounds then give ||grad A(u^{n+1},u^n)|| <= C(||u^{n+2}-u^{n+1}||+||u^{n+1}-u^n||) for a corrected constant C. Use this estimate in the global and local-rate proofs.
issues.why_classification: The old proof relies on incorrect derivatives, BDF coefficients, and an incorrect iterate of the M-term, so mathematical checking is required. All corrections follow by direct differentiation and substitution into the already stated update, however, and the same relative-error estimate and all affected conclusions survive with only changed constants. No new lemma or proof architecture is needed.

issues.title: Inverted sufficient-decrease coefficient in the smooth KL step
issues.failure_explanation: If the valid descent coefficient is \(q=(\alpha\lambda_{\min}+c)/(1+\lambda_{\max})^2\), the descent estimate gives \(A_n-A_{n+1}\ge q\|u^{n+2}-u^{n+1}\|^2\). The old ineq:KL_of_psi instead prints the reciprocal \(1/q\), which is not implied for general admissible parameters. Its following finite-length constant must consequently use \(1/q\), not \(q\).
issues.overall_effect: Even after repairing the relative-error calculation, the printed inequality does not establish finite length or the local-rate recursion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: If q > 0 is the valid sufficient-decrease coefficient satisfying A_n-A_{n+1} >= q||u^{n+1}-u^n||^2, replace the final coefficient in ineq:KL_of_psi by q, not 1/q. Combining this with the relative-error bound gives a subsequent finite-length constant proportional to C_L/q rather than q. Propagate that corrected constant through the finite-length and local-rate estimates.
issues.why_classification: The reciprocal printed in the KL step is not implied and is used in the following calculation, so the issue is substantive rather than transcriptional. Its resolution is nevertheless a local, routine correction of an inequality and its constants; it preserves finite length, convergence, and the rate statements without any mathematical weakening.

issues.title: Wrong sublinear-rate exponent
issues.failure_explanation: The old item (iii) states \(n^{-(1-\theta)/(2\theta-2)}\). Since \(2\theta-2<0\), its displayed power is positive and does not express decay. The appendix instead derives \(\rho=(1-\theta)/(2\theta-1)>0\) and bounds the error by a constant times \(n^{-\rho}\).
issues.overall_effect: The formal theorem fails to state the sublinear decay rate actually derived, although the underlying convergence result is unaffected by this statement typo.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exponent in item (iii) by -(1-theta)/(2 theta-1), so the bound reads ||u^n-u^*|| < c_2 n^{-(1-theta)/(2 theta-1)}.
issues.why_classification: The appendix in the old source explicitly derives rho = (1-theta)/(2 theta-1) and the bound n^{-rho}. Thus the theorem’s denominator 2 theta-2 is a uniquely identifiable transcription error; the proof and every underlying convergence claim already use the correct exponent.

issues.title: Mis-scaled extrapolated preconditioner
issues.failure_explanation: The old specialized update contains \(2M(y^n-\tilde u^n)/\delta t\), whereas the algorithmic subproblem and eq:solve:y:pre:general require \(M(y^n-\tilde u^n)\). It therefore specifies a differently scaled proximal metric. The coefficients \(5/(3\delta t)\) and \(1/(3\delta t)\) in the ensuing energy estimates are consequences of that mismatched construction.
issues.overall_effect: The extrapolated procedure analyzed in the old section is not the extrapolated specialization of the stated algorithm, so its descent, square-summability, and global-convergence chain does not certify the advertised construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize the metric consistently. Introduce P as the actual proximal metric and set the old section’s matrix M0 = (delta t/2)P. Then eq:til:yn becomes the exact algorithmic update with P(y^n-tilde u^n). Rewrite the dependent M0-norm terms mechanically using ||z||_{M0}^2 = (delta t/2)||z||_P^2; for example, the coefficients 5/(3 delta t) and 1/(3 delta t) become 5/6 and 1/6. Apply the same substitution in the corollary, Lyapunov function, square-summability theorem, and global theorem.
issues.why_classification: The proof coefficients depend on the inconsistent normalization, so this is not merely a copied symbol. However, positive scaling gives a bijection between positive-semidefinite metrics: after the stated renaming, the old estimates are exactly the estimates for the algorithm’s actual metric. The propagation is routine algebra, preserves the full class of preconditioners and all convergence guarantees, and requires no new argument.

issues.title: Incorrect M-norm rescaling in extrapolated square summability
issues.failure_explanation: From eq:LSstep, \(d^n=(u^{n+1}-u^n)/(1+\lambda_n)\), hence \(\|d^n\|_M^2=\|u^{n+1}-u^n\|_M^2/(1+\lambda_n)^2\). The old eq:minmax:control prints \(5/[3\delta t(1+\lambda_n)]\) and introduces a compensating unsquared factor on the previous step. Those terms do not follow from the preceding inequality, so the telescoping M-metric estimate is invalid.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish extrapolated square summability, and the extrapolated global theorem loses its stated decay input and auxiliary-energy monotonicity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use ||d^n||_M^2 = ||u^{n+1}-u^n||_M^2/(1+lambda_n)^2 everywhere. In the old normalization, the M-terms in the one-step estimate become 5||u^{n+1}-u^n||_M^2/[3 delta t(1+lambda_n)^2] - ||u^n-u^{n-1}||_M^2/(3 delta t). Define the corresponding Lyapunov function with M-term ||x-y||_M^2/(3 delta t); then the residual coefficient is [5/(1+lambda_max)^2-1]/(3 delta t), which is positive under lambda_max < sqrt(5)-1. Telescope this corrected estimate and use the corrected auxiliary function in the global theorem.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes an invalid norm-rescaling inference and therefore needs a mathematical correction. Squaring the denominator and matching the preceding-step coefficient in the Lyapunov function restores the same square-summability and global-convergence chain by routine algebra, with only auxiliary constants changed and no loss of scope or guarantee.

issues.title: Inconsistent auxiliary residual in the extrapolated KL proof
issues.failure_explanation: The old auxiliary contains \((1+\lambda_{\max})\|x-y\|_M^2/(3\delta t)\), whose gradient contribution is \(2(1+\lambda_{\max})M(x-y)/(3\delta t)\). The proof instead sets \(\tilde M=(1+\lambda_{\max})M/(6\delta t)\). Later it couples the decrement from \(\tilde A(u^n,u^{n-1})\) to \(\tilde A(u^{n+1},u^n)\) with a gradient at \((u^{n+1},u^n)\), although the displayed KL derivative is evaluated at the preceding energy. Thus no valid same-iterate relative-error/KL inequality is obtained.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not establish the vanishing auxiliary residual or the finite-length conclusion in parts (i) and (iii) of the extrapolated global theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Differentiate the auxiliary M-term exactly: if its coefficient is a_M, its gradient contribution is 2a_M M(x-y); for the printed auxiliary this is 2(1+lambda_max)M(x-y)/(3 delta t). Use the exact optimality equation at the same iteration to obtain the relative-error bound. Then set Z_n=(u^{n+1},u^n) and apply the KL inequality at Z_n to the decrement tilde A(Z_n)-tilde A(Z_{n+1}), rather than pairing that decrement with a gradient at another iterate. This yields the standard finite-length recursion and restores parts (i) and (iii).
issues.why_classification: The displayed gradient coefficient and the KL iterate pairing are invalid, so the proof cannot stand literally. Both are local differentiation and indexing corrections, and the smooth KL proof already present in the old source supplies the same-iterate template. Correcting them preserves the auxiliary-residual and finite-length conclusions with changed constants but no new proof architecture or weakening.

issues.title: Wrong linear-system coefficient in the SGS construction

failure_location.quote: Supposing $h(u) = Au-b_0$ as in Proposition \ref{prop:proximal_to_pre}, the discrete matrix of the linear operator  $T=\frac{3}{2\delta t}I + A$ is $D-E-E^T$ where $D$ is the diagonal part and $-E$ represents the strictly lower triangular part.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the matrix split used for SGS represents \(T=3I/(2\delta t)+A\). The old paper actually establishes in prop:proximal_to_pre that the subproblem has \(T=2I/\delta t+A\), and the later order proof also uses that value. The difference changes the diagonal matrix and hence the SGS preconditioner, so the prose specifies a materially different linear system.
issues.overall_effect: Following the prose literally constructs an SGS preconditioner for the wrong system, although prop:second_order:pre remains independently supported because its proof uses the correct coefficient.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace T = 3I/(2 delta t) + A in the SGS prose by T = 2I/(delta t) + A, and take D, E, and the SGS preconditioner from that corrected matrix.
issues.why_classification: Proposition prop:proximal_to_pre and the subsequent order proof both uniquely define T = 2I/(delta t) + A and already use that coefficient. The isolated prose coefficient is therefore a transcription error; correcting it requires no new preconditioning argument and does not affect the independently supported proposition.

issues.title: Extra SCAD factor in the BDCA comparison splitting
issues.failure_explanation: The old comparator construction expands to \(\frac12\|Au-b\|^2+\mu\mathcal H_\alpha(u)-\mu\tilde P(u)\), not the stated objective \(\frac12\|Au-b\|^2+\mu\mathcal H_\alpha(u)-\tilde P(u)\). Unless \(\mu=1\) or \(\tilde P=0\), it therefore defines a different BDCA/DCA comparison problem.
issues.overall_effect: The written BDCA and DCA comparator procedures do not solve eq:lsp, so the numerical comparison is not reproducible as a comparison on the stated objective from the displayed specification alone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the extra factor mu multiplying tilde P in eq:another:split. The comparator splitting should be E(u) = mu H_alpha(u) + (L/2)||u||^2 - [(L/2)||u||^2 + tilde P(u) - (1/2)||Au-b||^2], and the BDCA/DCA implementations should use this same displayed splitting.
issues.why_classification: Expanding the old display immediately contradicts the stated objective eq:lsp, while deleting the single extra factor gives exactly that objective and retains a valid DC splitting. The surrounding model and explicit claim that the comparators solve eq:lsp uniquely force this correction; no proof, new construction, or mathematical guarantee must be replaced.
